claim: [L279-L288] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Roller source and dissipation updates divide twice by sqrt(cx^2+cy^2) without guarding zero propagation speed.
other_wording: [L279-L288] (HIGH/division by zero) Both the roller update and reported roller dissipation divide by directional phase-speed magnitude without a positive floor.

claim: [L143-L147] (HIGH/stability timestep) The x-advection timestep denominator uses maxval(cgx) rather than maxval(abs(cgx)), so an all-negative x velocity field selects the 1e-10 floor and an excessively large timestep.
other_wording: [L145-L147] (HIGH/CFL calculation) The cross-shore CFL denominator uses maxval(cgx) rather than maxval(abs(cgx)), so a field of large negative propagation velocities yields an excessively large timestep.

claim: [L393-L426] (MED/boundary initialization) Fy is assigned only on interior i rows and j=1:ny, while its offshore/onshore and final lateral boundary rows are explicitly left unset by commented-out boundary copies.
other_wording: [L393-L426] (MED/stale force boundaries) Several Fy boundary entries are deliberately not assigned, so the saved model state can retain values from an earlier stationary solve rather than a defined boundary condition.

claim: [L203-L219,L397-L410,L557-L570] (HIGH/circular statistics) Mean wave direction is calculated as an arithmetic weighted mean of angles, which gives a direction near zero for energy straddling the -pi/+pi wrap instead of the correct circular mean.
other_wording: [L202-L220, L397-L410, L557-L570] (HIGH/wave-direction calculation) Both modes use arithmetic mean angles that fail across 0/2π, and stationary Snell refraction passes an unclamped value to asin.

claim: [L620-L643] (HIGH/convergence metric) Relative height convergence divides by s%H with no zero guard, while the EE branches populate wetmask but never apply it and therefore do not implement their apparent wet-cell-only contract.
other_wording: [L620-L643] (HIGH/convergence metric defects) Relative H error divides by zero wave height, while the EE metrics build a wetmask but never apply it, allowing dry or halo cells to control convergence.

claim: [L294-L300,L357-L363] (MED/numerical robustness) Wave action conversion divides wet-cell energy by sigm without any positive-frequency guard.
other_wording: [L294-L300] (HIGH/unguarded action conversion) Wet-cell energy is divided by s%sigm without checking for a positive intrinsic frequency.

claim: [L70-L114] (MED/persistent allocation/dispatch) callType has no default validation and saved work arrays are sized only on the first call, so a later call with a different grid or ntheta_local reuses incompatible shapes.
other_wording: [L70-L122] (HIGH/call-mode-dependent saved shape) Common saved arrays are dimensioned using the first callType's direction count and never resized, although the routine is designed to be called in both stationary and directions modes with potentially different ntheta values.

claim: [L601-L610] (HIGH/dimensional/state consistency) After scaling directional roller energy by gammafac squared, s%R is assigned RH*gammafac, a wave-height quantity, instead of a consistently scaled roller energy.
other_wording: [L599-L610] (HIGH/dimensionally incorrect roller state) After scaling rr by a height-based gamma factor, s%R is assigned RH*gammafac, a length, rather than the corresponding roller energy or the sum of scaled rr.

claim: [L509-L514] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Roller dissipation divides by sqrt(cx^2+cy^2) without guarding zero propagation speed.
other_wording: [L509-L514] (HIGH/division by zero) Roller dissipation divides by directional phase-speed magnitude without a positive floor.

claim: [L56-L72] (MED/numerical robustness) Although hhw is protected against dry or negative depth, gamma is computed with the unclamped s%hh, so zero-depth cells can produce infinities or NaNs in hstokes.
other_wording: [L64-L73] (HIGH/dry-cell division) The new hstokes path computes H/hh across the full grid without a positive depth floor, so dry zero-depth cells can produce invalid gamma and zero hstokes.

claim: [L1280-L1314] (HIGH/uninitialized indexing) Nbin is never initialized and directions equal to the upper bin edge or still outside the opposite edge after wrapping receive no assignment before maxval and array indexing use.
other_wording: [L1280-L1337] (HIGH/uninitialized directional-bin indices) Nbin is never initialized, and a direction shifted once by 2π can still fall outside a computational sector narrower than 2π, leaving its bin entry undefined before maxval and nspr handling.

claim: [L1789-L1794] (HIGH/vector rotation) Curvilinear flux rotation derives direction with atan(qy/max(qx,eps)), which clamps negative qx and cannot preserve the correct quadrant.
other_wording: [L1789-L1794] (HIGH/curvilinear rotation quadrant loss) Flux rotation derives its angle from atan(qy/max(qx,eps)), which replaces every negative qx with a positive epsilon and therefore gives incorrect quadrants and components.

claim: [L260,L311,L1016-L1017,L1057-L1059,L1194-L1205,L1922-L1932] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Zero wave height is accepted but multiple subsequent spectral normalizations and representative-period calculations divide by zero.
other_wording: [L1194-L1210] (HIGH/zero-energy rescaling) Hm0 correction divides by hm0now and directional-width construction divides by S0 without a zero-energy contract; the small S0 floor does not protect hm0now.

claim: [L69-L89,L107-L118,L478-L489,L502-L533,L613-L666,L801-L850] (HIGH/MPI state distribution) Master-only input populates testc, dimensions, switches, factors, and spectrum arrays while all corresponding broadcasts are commented out, leaving non-master ranks to branch on uninitialized values, allocate with undefined extents, and compute from undefined data.
other_wording: [L69-L86] (HIGH/non-master undefined state) testc is read only by the master but is tested on every rank to set saved reuse, with the corresponding broadcasts explicitly commented out.

claim: [L1453-L1454] (LOW/statistics) The standard-deviation denominators use size(array-1), which equals N rather than the apparently intended N-1.
other_wording: [L1453-L1454] (LOW/standard-deviation denominator) The expressions size(array-1) return the full sample count rather than size(array)-1 as the surrounding standard-deviation comments imply.

claim: [L465-L472,L627-L650] (MED/input error handling) The SWAN keyword-search loops have no I/O status checks, so malformed or truncated files can loop indefinitely or repeatedly read past EOF.
other_wording: [L465-L472, L627-L649] (HIGH/unbounded malformed-input loop) SWAN keyword searches perform reads without IOSTAT or EOF handling and can loop indefinitely on a truncated or malformed file.

claim: [L1703-L1709] (HIGH/direction calculation) Bound-wave direction uses atan(KKy/KKx) rather than atan2, losing the quadrant whenever KKx is negative.
other_wording: [L1703-L1709] (HIGH/direction quadrant loss) Difference-wave direction uses atan(KKy/KKx) with a signed epsilon instead of atan2, losing the correct quadrant whenever KKx is negative.

claim: [L517-L593,L817-L835] (MED/bounds/input validation) Both SWAN and variance-density readers dereference theta(2) without validating ndir>=2.
other_wording: [L474-L593, L723-L749, L805-L881] (MED/spectral-axis validation) SWAN and VarDens inputs are used without requiring at least two directions or strictly increasing frequency and direction axes, despite direct second-element indexing, quadrature, and interpolation.

claim: [L157-L162] (HIGH/bounds/numerical robustness) The ny>0 branch uses slices 2:ny, so ny=1 produces empty sums and division by zero instead of using the single offshore point.
other_wording: [L157-L162] (MED/empty weighted average) For a minimal 2-D grid with ny=1, the offshore-depth average uses empty slices and divides by a zero sum.

claim: [L463-L498,L733-L765] (HIGH/spectrum-axis handling) The SWAN frequency-conversion branch is a no-op and never repairs descending or relative-frequency input before moment integration and frequency-range calculations assume an increasing absolute axis.
other_wording: [L463-L498] (HIGH/unimplemented frequency conversion) SWAN RFREQ input is recognized but its conversion to absolute frequency is a no-op.

claim: [L1016-L1036] (HIGH/degenerate spectrum) If the selected frequency range has one bin, M or wp%K can be one and the code divides by M, wp%K-1, and the resulting zero df.
other_wording: [L981-L1036, L1872-L1905] (HIGH/empty/degenerate spectral range) An empty threshold range makes M zero and a single-bin range makes K=1 and df=0, causing divisions by M, K-1, and df.

claim: [L1367-L1457] (HIGH/order-dependent physics) The total envelope and directional weights are computed inside the directional-bin loop before later bins' zeta values exist, so Ampzeta for early bins depends on processing order and omits later directional components.

[L2990-L3008] (HIGH/boundary-file schema) When time-step interpolation is active, qinterp has only three fields and the writer omits the fourth elevation field even though the direct-access record length and non-interpolated path use four fields.
other_wording: [L2982-L3009] (HIGH/direct-access record shape) When dtchanged is true qinterp has only three fields although the file record length and reader contract are four fields, unlike the non-interpolated write of q(:,:,:).

claim: [L3524-L3529] (HIGH/layer averaging) The 3D second-order update divides the first-layer flux by z (negative) and the second by h0+z, inconsistent with the layer thicknesses and with the earlier short-wave implementation that uses h0+z for layer 1 and -z for layer 2.
other_wording: [L3524-L3528] (HIGH/incorrect layer flux conversion) Second-order layer flux is converted using q1/z and q2/(h0+z), even though z is negative and the lower and upper layer thicknesses are h0+z and -z respectively.

claim: [L2006-L2098] (HIGH/allocation/runtime) wp%PRindex is allocated inside the offshore-point loop, so the second iteration attempts to allocate an already-associated pointer.
other_wording: [L2006-L2098] (HIGH/repeated pointer allocation) wp%PRindex is allocated inside the offshore-point loop, so the second point attempts to allocate an already-associated pointer.

claim: [L489,L641,L1495,L1512,L1637] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Hm0=0 is explicitly accepted, but the resulting zero spectrum reaches unguarded normalizations and weighted means whose denominators are zero.
other_wording: [L627-L641] (MED/singular shallow-depth formula) The TMA correction divides by tanh(k*h0) and normalizes by sqrt(sum(y)) without guarding zero boundary depth or a collapsed spectrum.

claim: [L3341-L3342] (MED/filtering/indexing) The high-wavenumber cutoff tests only k3(m,1), but rows m>K+1 populate columns ii>1 while column 1 remains zero, so those higher rows evade the cutoff.
other_wording: [L3271-L3342] (HIGH/wrong cutoff index) The superharmonic cutoff tests k3(m,1), but for m>K+1 valid entries start above column 1 and k3(m,1) remains its initialized zero, disabling the intended cutoff.

claim: [L3411-L3417] (HIGH/scientific formula) The upper-layer qx2/qy2 ratios subtract sinh(KKx) or sinh(KKy) with no depth factor, unlike the surrounding dimensionless sinh(k*depth) terms, producing dimensionally inconsistent layer partitioning.
other_wording: [L3413, L3417] (HIGH/dimensionally inconsistent layer formula) The upper-layer ratios subtract sinh(KKx) or sinh(KKy) rather than an interface-depth product, leaving a dimensioned wavenumber as a hyperbolic-function argument and omitting z.

claim: [L965-L998,L1038-L1046,L1311-L1335] (HIGH/spectrum-axis handling) The SWAN reader acknowledges that frequencies are often non-monotone but performs only no-op assignments, after which interpolation and integration assume ordered endpoints and can reject or negatively integrate a descending frequency axis.
other_wording: [L978-L990, L1175-L1203, L1327-L1336, L1353-L1356] (HIGH/axis/interpolation mismatch) The readers do not sort or reject nonmonotone axes—even noting that SWAN frequencies are often nonmonotone—while endpoint range tests and linear_interp calls assume an ordered frequency axis.

claim: [L2064-L2068] (MED/numerical robustness) Spatial spectrum interpolation rescales by sfimp/sfnow without guarding sfnow=0.
other_wording: [L2061-L2068] (HIGH/zero interpolation divisor) Spatial spectral interpolation rescales by sfimp/sfnow without guarding sfnow=0.

claim: [L1015-L1046,L1189-L1203,L1132-L1143,L1239-L1250] (MED/bounds/input validation) Both spectrum readers index angular entries 1 and 2 without enforcing nang>=2, so a one-direction input can read out of bounds.
other_wording: [L980-L990, L1015-L1046, L1175-L1203, L1241-L1249] (HIGH/unchecked array extent) File-provided frequency and direction counts are not validated, while later code unconditionally accesses angle element 2 and adjacent-angle differences.

claim: [L172-L180,L593-L607,L1092,L1180-L1206] (HIGH/allocation/runtime) The external-time catch-up loop can call read_spectrum_input repeatedly on the same specin element, but each reader unconditionally allocates already-associated pointer components, causing an allocation failure when more than one spectrum interval is skipped.
other_wording: [L172-L181, L593-L607, L691, L984, L1019, L1092, L1180, L1193, L1206] (HIGH/reallocation of associated pointers) The catch-up loop can call a spectrum reader repeatedly on the same spectrum object, but the readers allocate its pointer components again without first deallocating or nullifying them.

claim: [L3348-L3350] (HIGH/indexing/phase) Second-order component phases use Findex(1)+ii rather than Findex(1)+ii-1 (or Findex(ii)), shifting every primary component by one frequency bin and reading beyond the generated-component span for ii=K.
other_wording: [L3348-L3350] (HIGH/off-by-one Fourier index) Superharmonic phases access Findex(1)+ii and +jj instead of the component indices Findex(ii) and Findex(jj), shifting every lookup and reaching beyond the last generated component.

claim: [L1637-L1657] (MED/sampling/CDF) The PDF is normalized by its simple sum but its CDF is then formed with trapezoidal half-endpoint weights, leaving the last CDF value below one and sending some uniform random draws outside the CDF interpolation range.
other_wording: [L1637-L1657] (HIGH/CDF construction) The trapezoidal cumulative directional distribution is not normalized after integration, so its final value is generally below one although draws span the full [0,1) interval.

claim: [L1567-L1572] (HIGH/scientific formula) The nonhydrostatic cutoff frequency is computed as g*k*tanh(kh)/(2*pi), omitting the square root required by the dispersion relation and yielding dimensionally incorrect frequency filtering.
other_wording: [L1569-L1572] (HIGH/dispersion formula) The nonhydrostatic frequency cutoff assigns g*k*tanh(kh)/(2*pi) without the square root required to convert dispersion-relation omega-squared to frequency.

claim: [L3436-L3441,L3524-L3530] (MED/missing state update) Second-order 3D generation computes qy1 and qy2 fields but the accumulation branch updates only uits and duits, leaving vits and dvits without the corresponding transverse second-order contribution.
other_wording: [L3436-L3441, L3524-L3530] (HIGH/discarded transverse velocity) The second-order routine computes qy1 and qy2 time series but never adds them to vits or dvits when assembling the nonhydrostatic boundary signal.

claim: [L1939-L1959] (HIGH/numerical robustness) Wave-train variance rescales by (hm0/hm0post)^2 without guarding hm0post=0, which occurs when the selected component frequency range contains no energy for a location.
other_wording: [L1956-L1959] (HIGH/zero normalization divisor) Per-location variance is rescaled by (hm0/hm0post)^2 without checking hm0post, which can be zero for a location with no selected-frequency energy.

claim: [L3226-L3242,L3407-L3418,L3434-L3441] (HIGH/branch-condition/runtime) Allocation of six-field 3D arrays requires nonhq3d==1 and nhlay>0, but later use tests only nonhq3d==1, so nonhq3d==1 with nhlay<=0 accesses unallocated qx/qy arrays and fields 5-6 of four-field arrays.
other_wording: [L3226-L3242, L3406-L3418, L3434-L3447] (HIGH/allocation/branch mismatch) Six-field storage and qx/qy layer arrays are allocated only when nonhq3d=1 and nhlay>0, but later branches test only nonhq3d=1 and can access those arrays when they were never allocated.

claim: [L125-L131,L331-L332] (MED/state/output contract) The routine increments bccount before the final-timestep early return, and that return leaves the INTENT(OUT) curline unassigned while also consuming a boundary-condition sequence number.
other_wording: [L125-L130] (HIGH/output/state contract) The last-step early return occurs after incrementing bccount and before assigning the INTENT(OUT) curline, so the caller receives an undefined line while the global sequence advances.
